capabilities: Reorder blocks via drag and drop
Convert block types using slash commands
disambiguation: Not a standard text editor; it transforms notes into structured, block-based content with advanced layout and manipulation features.
extras: Only available on desktop; licensed under MIT.
problem: Obsidian lacks native block-based editing features like block handles, drag-and-drop reordering, and structured content tools such as columns and block IDs.
summary: A Notion-style block editor that adds block handles, drag-and-drop reordering, multi-select, type conversion, and advanced column management to Obsidian.
